facts.text: Casas is a rural unincorporated community located about seven miles northwest of Rio Grande City in an arid brushland region.
Early settlement in the Casas area reflects Spanish colonial initiatives along the Rio Grande from the mid-eighteenth century.
The terrain of Casas consists of flat to gently rolling plains with deep loamy soils and clayey subsoils.
Casas sits in a humid subtropical climate zone with hot, humid summers and mild winters without prolonged cold spells.
Ranching dominated the local economy for decades, with cattle numbers in the region peaking at over eighty-five thousand in 1910.
Oil exploration brought significant economic activity to the area, with county production exceeding two hundred sixteen million barrels between 1929 and 1970.
